title: The impact of applying challenge-based gamification program on students’ learning outcomes: Academic achievement, motivation and flow
reason: Randomised control vs experimental comparison of a challenge-based gamified web program (Educhall) on achievement, self-reported motivation and flow. Only group contrasts (ANCOVA, MANOVA, t-test); no per-student platform activity measure is analysed.

extraction.n_quote: The study applied a random experimental research design within distance learning context with 30 university students of control group and 30 students of experimental group
extraction.population: university students in a distance-learning course
extraction.lms_indicators: none analysed (Educhall quiz/challenge use not measured per student)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: academic achievement test; motivation (ARCS: attention, relevance, confidence, satisfaction; self-report); flow (self-report)
extraction.notes: n is the sum of 30 + 30. Group effects (achievement partial eta2 = 0.30; motivation partial eta2 = 0.27) are treatment contrasts, not indicator-outcome relations.
